correctness.rationale: For Cay(F₂⁴,{e1,e2,e3,e4,e1+e2+e3+e4}), independently rebuild all 16 neighborhoods. Each neighbor set is of size five and their face closure has 352 nonempty faces with f=(16,80,160,80,16). XOR adjacency is checked to be strongly regular (16,5,0,2). The actual proposed nontrivial toggle order (9,11,0,5,4,14,3,2,12,8,13,6,15,7,10,1) gives 160 disjoint Morse incidence pairs; all 1040 Hasse incidences form a directed acyclic graph. The only critical faces are one 0-cell and thirty-one 2-cells, forcing wedge 31 S²; no mod-p homology shortcut is used. Lovász connectivity of this wedge supports χ(C)≥4, consistent with given explicit 4-coloring.

value.rationale: The Clebsch graph is a canonical strongly regular graph and folded 5-cube, and its Lovász neighborhood complex is a central topological object in coloring lower bounds. The exact wedge (not just Euler characteristic or chromatic number), with explicit acyclic matching, clarifies why the Lovász bound is sharp for this natural test graph; finite exact topology is useful on its own.
